company: Bold Military Technology and Defense Industry Inc.
usageGuideIntro: All modules and buttons are grouped below with their exact purpose.
aboutUsBody: Bold Military Technology and Defense Industry Inc. develops sovereign solutions in defense and decision-support technologies. BQI is its quantum-powered decision intelligence platform for real-time strategic decision support.
missionBody: To provide decision-makers with real-time, multi-dimensional, reliable intelligence across defense, economy, energy, and social domains.
visionBody: To make quantum computing an integral part of national security strategy.
contactBody: For questions about the system, please contact the center. For emergencies, use the Emergency Center button inside the app.
settingsPushUnsupported: This browser does not support push notifications.
securityPasskeyIntro: Sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, or your device's biometrics instead of your password. Your biometric data never leaves your device or reaches this app.
securityPasskeyUnsupported: This browser or device does not support passkeys.
securityPasskeyRemoveConfirmBody: "{name}" will no longer be able to sign in to this account. This cannot be undone, but you can always add a new passkey later.
securityDeviceForgetHint: Removes this device's offline login authorization.
securityDeviceForgetConfirmBody: This will remove this device's offline login authorization. You'll need to sign in again with an internet connection to use offline login again.
securityDeviceForgetSuccess: This device's offline login authorization has been removed.
errDeviceNotAuthorizedOffline: This device has not been authorized online for this account yet.
errNoOfflineSession: No offline login credential exists yet for this device. Please sign in online with your password first.
errTooManyOfflineAttempts: Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.
errOfflineSessionExpired: The offline session has expired. Please sign in again with an internet connection.
appModeOfflineConfirmBody: Cloud connectivity, live sync, and online-only services will be temporarily suspended. Your local data and pending changes are preserved.
securityPasskeyOfflineModeHint: Passkey actions are unavailable in offline mode.
localAIModeNativeHint: When enabled, analysis and consultation requests use the local engine even if the cloud is reachable.
localAIModeWebHint: The browser can save the preference; the real local engine runs in the desktop and Android apps.
localAIWebUnavailable: This browser session has no downloadable local model. Use the desktop or Android app for local generation.
localAIIntro: Download an offline AI model to this device so consultation still works without an internet connection. Nothing is downloaded until you tap Download.
localAINotCapable: This device does not meet the recommended minimum to run the model reliably; it may run slowly or not at all.
localAITierSwitchConfirm: Switching models will remove the currently installed model (downloaded file). Continue?
hardwareVerifiedBody: A report's IBM Quantum hardware verification finished and was added to the report.
hardwareVerifiedFailedBody: IBM Quantum hardware verification was attempted but did not produce a result.
analysisCompletedBody: Your requested analysis finished and was saved to history.

guideModules: 1) Top Bar and Left Menu

The live date/time opens a calendar.|CHAT opens voice/text consultation.|HISTORY opens saved reports.|NOTIFICATIONS shows chat, emergency and system events.|USER MANAGEMENT is only visible to admin users.|MENU opens this guide, About, Mission & Vision and Contact.|SETTINGS controls language, sound, push notifications, theme and sidebar appearance.|LOGOUT securely ends the session.|The left menu holds HOME, NEW ANALYSIS and the analysis categories; PERSONNEL RADAR appears in the System Status panel for admin users only.
2) Home & System Status

The live map, morning brief and activity feed provide the operational overview.|SYSTEM STATUS uses live backend health data and shows these exact labels:|PLATFORM: CHECK (checking) / OFF (unreachable) / READY / LIMITED (partially ready).|AI: CHECK / READY / OFF.|DATABASE: CHECK / N/A (not configured) / ONLINE / OFF.|IBM Q: READY (real IBM hardware configured) / LOCAL (local Qiskit Aer simulator in use).|STORAGE: OBJECT (persistent object storage) / LOCAL.|REDIS: ONLINE / MEMORY (local fallback).|If location permission was granted, the same screen shows a live weather widget (refreshed every 10 minutes).
3) Analysis Categories

Choose the domain before starting: Defense, Energy, Offensive, Economy, Social Events, Consultation, Health, Multi-Domain, BDDK and BTK.|Unlike these categories, Cyber Intelligence (BCI) and BFI Systemic Risk are separate command centres with their own pages (see the BCI and BFI sections).|BDDK and BTK are two fully separate categories, distinct from the other eight; their status badge reads "Quantum" because they work with real transaction data in quantum mode (see Quantum Analysis with Real Data).|Users do not need to choose internal AI or quantum engines — this is handled automatically.
4) Create an Analysis & Upload Files

Enter a clear report title and analysis brief; use speech-to-text where available.|Attach Source File to upload PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, XLS/XLSX or images (jpg/png/gif/webp/svg/bmp), up to 20MB.|Images are sent directly to AI vision analysis; PDF/DOCX/TXT are converted to text and included in the analysis.|CSV/Excel files are automatically classified into one of three structures — a transaction table, a scenario table, or a resource-allocation (optimization) table — based on which columns are present.|GENERATE DETAILED ANALYSIS REPORT runs the standard workflow; provider fallback, provenance and trace metadata are managed automatically.
5) Quantum Analysis with Real Data

With quantum mode on, BDDK/BTK categories accept a real transaction ledger (CSV/Excel); required columns are "Amount" and either "Hour" or "Date", up to 500 rows.|If uploaded, the quantum engine scores these real transactions instead of AI-generated sample records; the AI is explicitly instructed not to invent or alter this table.|Other categories accept real scenario data ("Scenario"/"Probability" columns) or a resource-allocation table ("Item"/"Value"/"Cost" columns with a budget percentage); if uploaded, the quantum engine uses this real data instead of an AI estimate.|A green confirmation chip appears after a successful upload (e.g. "✓ N real transaction records loaded"); any column issues are listed as amber warnings and the chip can be removed with ×.
6) Quantum Analysis Results

QUANTUM PROBABILITY MODE supports multi-scenario analysis, fraud/anomaly detection, or resource optimization.|The result header shows, depending on the active engine: backend name, qubit count and shot count for scenarios; backend, qubits and flagged/total transaction count for fraud detection; backend, qubits and budget percentage used for optimization.|Three charts with a table/graph toggle are available: Scenario Comparison (AI estimate vs. quantum result with confidence interval), Quantum Anomaly Detection (flagged vs. normal transaction risk scores), and Quantum Resource Allocation Optimization (selected vs. unselected items).|The authoritative result always follows the deterministic local path; real IBM hardware, when configured, runs as an independent verification lane — manual classical/quantum comparison is not required.
7) Scenario Deep Dive

In the QUANTUM PROBABILITY MATRIX section, every alternative scenario (other than the primary one) has its own ANALYZE button.|Clicking it generates a separate, complete report for that scenario; the view switches to an ALTERNATIVE SCENARIO ANALYSIS header with its own DOCX/PDF download and share options.|Use "← Back to Main Report" to return to the primary result.
8) Reports, Downloads & Sharing

Review reports on screen; use DOWNLOAD .DOCX and DOWNLOAD .PDF to download, and SHARE to share.|The voice-output button reads the report aloud.|Use descriptive titles for archive clarity.|Hardware verification confirms that a real IBM job ran; it does not prove institutional origin of the input.
9) History
HISTORY has a "Search by title or content…" box and a category filter dropdown.|Each card offers view, download DOCX, download PDF and share actions.|Older reports may contain less audit metadata.
10) Analysis Audit

Opening a report can show an Analysis Audit panel with: AI provider, Model, Prompt version, Data source, Data quality (score/100), Classification, Analysis duration, Quantum backend, Quantum shots, Created.|This panel is cloud-only; on desktop/native builds viewing offline history, the Audit panel is not shown.|A missing field means that metadata was not recorded and must not be treated as verified.
11) Offline Use & Sync

On desktop/native builds, HISTORY is read from the device's local SQLite database; the Analysis Audit panel is not available in this mode.|A badge at the bottom shows Q LOCAL / SYNC / Q CLOUD — this tracks actual connectivity automatically.|Turning on Offline Mode under Settings → Connection manually stops cloud sync and background services; while it's on, the badge always reads "Q LOCAL · MANUAL" regardless of real connectivity, and stays that way until you switch back to Automatic.|Switching back to Automatic checks connectivity, prompts for re-login if your session expired, and syncs any pending changes automatically.|Logging out keeps this device's offline-login authorization intact: you can log back in with the same password with no internet; Forget This Device, under Settings → Security, removes that authorization entirely — after that, offline login requires a fresh online login first.|If Forget This Device is used while Offline Mode is active, local offline-login authorization is removed immediately; the server record is safely reconciled with a fresh session token on the next successful online login to the same account. Returning to Auto mode alone never sends an old credential.|This toggle is separate from Prefer Local AI under Settings → Local AI: that setting only decides whether consultation/analysis generation runs on the local engine or the cloud AI, and doesn't affect the app's overall connectivity or sync behavior.|If a record was edited on two devices while offline, a Sync Conflict window opens, showing the local and cloud versions side by side; choose "Use local version" or "Use cloud version" to resolve it.|If your session needs re-authentication while offline, a banner appears asking you to log in again; local data is never lost, and pending changes sync once you're back in.|On desktop or Android, NEW ANALYSIS can still produce a full report with no internet: if a model was already downloaded from Settings → Local AI (chosen automatically by device RAM -- 0.5B/1.5B/7B on Android, 1.5B/7B on desktop), generation runs entirely on the device; the result is marked with a "Q LOCAL LLM (OFFLINE)" badge and is saved to HISTORY automatically.|If no model is downloaded, or generation fails, the app falls back to "Q LOCAL DATA" mode, which matches against your existing archived reports instead; .DOCX/.PDF download and share in this mode are generated on-device and are not identical in formatting to the cloud version.|Settings → Local AI also lets you manually pick a different tier (LOW/MID/HIGH) from the list -- it's shown whether or not a model is currently installed. Selecting a different tier removes the current model first, then the newly chosen tier is ready to download.
12) Location, Personnel Radar & Weather

The app asks for location permission only once, with an explicit consent prompt; nothing is shared if you decline.|If granted, location powers the weather widget on Home (refreshed every 10 minutes) and is streamed live to the server.|PERSONNEL RADAR is only visible to admin users; when opened, it shows the live locations of connected, consenting users on a map of Turkey.|Locations update live as devices move, not on a fixed timer; selecting a user offers an "Open in Google Maps" link.
13) Consultation & Voice Assistant (Persona & Memory)

VOICE uses microphone-driven consultation; CHAT uses text; auto-listen can resume after a response.|The persona selector switches between 8 assistant characters (General, Analyst, Diplomat, Hawk, Sage, Joker, Stoic, Angry), each with its own tone and voice; the choice is remembered.|The Memory panel lets you search, reload, archive or delete past conversations; conversations are auto-saved at the end of a session.|Voice commands can trigger many actions: going to Home, filling in category/title/brief, generating an analysis, toggling quantum mode, downloading a report, opening History or the guide, opening the emergency panel, and logging out.
14) Emergency Center & Notification Center

REPORT TO CENTER sends urgent information to the center; NOTIFY USERS broadcasts to active users when authorized; MESSAGING supports authenticated communication.|The Notification Center has All / Chat / Emergency / System filters, an unread counter, a sound on/off toggle and a volume slider; opening the panel marks everything as read.|When a report's IBM Quantum hardware verification completes, a separate system notification arrives; clicking it navigates directly to History.
15) Permissions, Roles & User Management (Admin)

Every analysis is automatically assigned a classification based on its category: Defense, Offensive, BDDK, BTK and Multi-Domain are CONFIDENTIAL, the rest are INTERNAL.|Your role (admin / analyst / viewer) determines which classifications you can access; you cannot create, view or download an analysis above your role's ceiling — that's the answer to "why can't I see this analysis".|Admins can add users; rename a user code; update nickname, email, password, and admin access; block or unblock users; and delete users from the User Management panel.|Email is optional; when supplied, it receives emergency, message, and video-meeting-start alerts while that user is offline.|The Activity Log tab lists all admin actions, and the Fraud Trend tab charts the BDDK/BTK flag rate over time.
16) Appearance & Troubleshooting

Settings > Appearance offers DARK, LIGHT and SYSTEM themes; SYSTEM follows the device appearance automatically and the choice is remembered.|READY/ONLINE means available; LIMITED/CHECK means the capability is degraded or being checked; LOCAL/MEMORY means a fallback is active; OFF/N/A means unavailable or not configured (see Home & System Status).|If generation fails, preserve the brief, check System Status and retry once.|For security, 15 minutes without activity triggers a warning and logout. The maximum online session is 2 hours for a standard user and 4 hours for an admin; expiry returns you to the login screen.|If asked to re-authenticate while offline, use "Log In Again" to continue — your local data is never lost.
17) Cyber Analysis (BCI)

Selecting the Cyber category opens the BCI module, a separate command center with its own tabs: Dashboard, Assets, Scans, Findings, Reports, Engines, Quantum & PQC, and admin-only Controlled Proof.|A scan only starts if the target is covered by an APPROVED authorization scope for the requested class; there is no way to scan an unauthorized target.|NEW ANALYSIS walks through a wizard: pick or create an Asset, review the auto-selected Engines (BCI chooses engines by scan class — there is no manual per-engine override), review the Quantum computation method if applicable, then start the scan and land on the Report step.|The Engines and Quantum & PQC tabs are reference panels only — they show the engine catalog with live health, and provider/organization policy status; they are not scan setup screens. Use New Analysis to actually select engines or a compute method for a scan.|Every wizard choice records its provenance: the BCI recommendation, what you selected, and what was actually used (including any fallback), so a decision can always be traced back.|Active scans can be Stopped, Inspected (to see live engine runs, findings, fuzz/resilience/intrusive results), or Archived; archiving hides a scan from the active list but never deletes its history — an archived scan can be restored from the Archive tab at any time.|Findings can be Explained, have a fix Verified, Confirmed, or marked as a false positive; each finding shows its risk, confidence, priority and verification status plus its source engines.|AI-generated assessments are structured and provenance-safe: each one carries a verdict (No findings / Needs review / Critical / Partial coverage), the scope actually covered, key evidence, known limitations, and a suggested next step — never an unqualified claim.|Reports show a content hash and an integrity flag (valid / TAMPERED) plus the BCI version that generated them.|Quantum & PQC also covers Post-Quantum Security: crypto/JWT discovery against authorized targets, the PQC Readiness Score, CBOM components, the crypto inventory, and a migration roadmap flagging harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure; quantum optimization is a separate, opt-in remediation step run against existing findings, never part of the scan itself.|Assets can be archived and restored the same way as scans; archiving only hides an asset from the active inventory, all of its scan and finding history is preserved.
18) BCI Engines — Passive & Safe-Active Scanning

BCI runs nine real engines, each tagged with an intrusiveness class that controls who can trigger it and what scope it needs: PASSIVE (read-only, no live traffic beyond a normal request), SAFE_ACTIVE (real requests against the target, never exploitation), and RESTRICTED (admin-only, requires an approved authorization scope for that exact class).|Trivy (PASSIVE — SCA, Secrets, IaC, Config) scans a repository or container image for known vulnerable dependencies, leaked secrets, and misconfigured infrastructure-as-code or config files.|OSV-Scanner (PASSIVE — SCA, Supply Chain) cross-checks every dependency in a repository against the OSV vulnerability database across all detected package ecosystems.|Semgrep (PASSIVE — SAST) runs static code analysis with a selectable ruleset — auto, default, security-audit, or OWASP Top Ten — to catch real code-level vulnerability patterns.|Nuclei (SAFE_ACTIVE — Web, API) sends real HTTP requests at a domain, subdomain, URL or API using official vulnerability templates, chosen by scan profile: STANDARD covers CVEs, misconfigurations and exposures; EXTENDED adds general vulnerabilities and technology fingerprinting; FULL_SAFE runs the entire safe template set. DoS, fuzzing, intrusive, brute-force, default-login and credential-stuffing templates are always excluded, whichever profile is chosen.|naabu (SAFE_ACTIVE — Network Discovery) discovers open ports on a domain, subdomain, IP or CIDR using a selectable port profile: top 100 ports, ports 1-1000, the full 1-65535 range, or a custom list.|BCI Posture Intelligence (PASSIVE) accepts cloud and security-posture snapshots through a validated schema, redacts sensitive values, and feeds them into the same normalized finding and decision pipeline.
19) BCI Smart Fuzz

Smart Fuzz (SAFE_ACTIVE) is BCI's own input-robustness engine: it first discovers real endpoints and parameters on the target — same-origin HTML links and forms, robots.txt, sitemap, and OpenAPI/Swagger definitions when present — instead of guessing blindly.|Every discovered GET parameter always receives BCI's own BASE test set: at least 8 real probes per parameter, covering empty/percent-encoded boundary values, integer edge cases (negative, zero, overflow, oversized), a long string, unicode, special characters, a path-traversal marker, a SQL-injection marker, a reflected-XSS marker, and a null literal. This minimum coverage always runs and can never be reduced.|An optional AI Adaptive layer — a separate, capped budget of up to 20 extra probes — may prioritize additional categories on specific parameters that BCI's own type inference didn't already cover. It can only add from this same fixed, reviewed payload catalog, never inject a value of its own, and it never replaces or shrinks the BASE set.|Response behavior — status code, body size, latency, and whether a reflected marker comes back unescaped — is compared against a real baseline request captured for that exact endpoint, not judged on status code alone.|Any discovered endpoint that mutates data (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) is reported as discovered-but-not-probed rather than actually sent fuzzed input — Smart Fuzz never performs a mutating request.
20) BCI Smart Intrusive

Smart Intrusive (RESTRICTED) only runs against a target explicitly covered by an APPROVED authorization scope for that class. Every result is tagged with where it came from: BASE (BCI's own automatic, always-run coverage), USER (a module an admin explicitly selected — an admin's explicit choice can never be blocked by an AI suggestion), or AI_ADAPTIVE (a module an AI proposal added on top, never in place of BASE or USER).|BCI decides which of its 13 implemented validation modules actually apply to a given target in real time — not every module runs against every target: CORS Validation (sends an untrusted Origin and checks whether it's reflected back, especially alongside Allow-Credentials), Security Header Behavior (checks whether security headers present on a normal response silently disappear elsewhere), Error Disclosure (looks for well-known stack-trace or debug-page markers leaking into a response), HTTP Method/Protocol Validation (cross-checks the Allow header against a real TRACE probe), Path Normalization (tests non-destructive path variants for proxy/backend normalization mismatches), Content-Type Negotiation (compares behavior across different Accept headers), Cache/Proxy Behavior (compares real cache metadata across repeated and unique-key requests without attempting cache poisoning), Host-Header Routing Validation (overrides the Host header on a real connection and compares the response), Rate-Limit Header Observation (a purely passive two-request check of whether rate-limit headers are advertised and accurate), WebSocket/Streaming Protocol Validation (a real RFC 6455 handshake with an untrusted Origin on WebSocket-like endpoints), OpenAPI/API Schema Behavior (validates real responses against the API's own declared schema), Technology-Specific Validation (fingerprints the stack and checks for exact version disclosure), and Finding Reproducibility (re-verifies a specific prior finding from any BCI engine to confirm it's real and not a false positive).|Every module performs a real network/HTTP action; none of them exploit a vulnerability or simulate a result — a module that can't actually run reports an ERROR, never a false PASS.
21) BCI Smart Resilience

Smart Resilience (RESTRICTED, capability DOS) is availability/load testing — a distinct capability from Smart Intrusive, gated the same way: admin-only, and only against a target with an APPROVED authorization scope for that exact class, with no separate second approval step.|Real, concurrent, rate-paced HTTP load is generated by BCI's own load engine (a persistent keep-alive connection pool, not one process per request), and every round is tagged BASE / USER / AI_ADAPTIVE exactly like Smart Intrusive — an admin's explicit module choice always runs, an AI proposal can only add on top.|BCI selects which of its implemented resilience modules apply to the target in real time: Baseline Performance (a sequential, no-load sample every other module compares against), Concurrency Validation (holds a concurrent connection level and measures success/latency), Sustained Load (a constant request rate for the full run), Spike and Burst Load (a low baseline with one short high-intensity window), Ramp-Up/Ramp-Down (gradually increases or decreases the rate), Rate-Limit Trigger Validation (a burst specifically to see whether 429/Retry-After actually fires), Timeout Behavior (load with a deliberately tight timeout to measure the real timeout rate), Recovery Validation (baseline, then burst, then measures how fully performance recovers), Capacity/Saturation Detection (a coarse ramp to find the approximate real throughput ceiling), Multi-Endpoint Load (spreads load across several already-discovered endpoints instead of one URL), Authenticated Load (applies a caller-supplied auth header to test authenticated-session capacity, not just anonymous endpoints), and Cross-Engine Targeted Resilience (applies load specifically to the endpoints named in findings from other BCI engines).|Nothing here is a denial-of-service attack in the destructive sense — every module measures real, bounded, admin-authorized behavior under load and stops at the plan's configured limits.
22) Controlled Proof of Impact (Admin)

Controlled Proof is admin-only and validates eligible scanner evidence with non-destructive deterministic checks against the target; it produces a result separate from a normal scan and finding record.|In Cyber Analysis > Controlled Proof, enter an authorized target URL and select Analyze. The view reports live-engine coverage, matched evidence, rejected-candidate reasons, the validator, security impact, and evidence hash.|History records can be inspected, archived, restored, deleted, and exported as PDF/DOCX. Deletion is permanent; archiving only hides a record from the active view.|When a supported provider is configured, a public-visibility proof can run for 5, 10, or 30 seconds. It is a timed, reversible validation marker; it neither changes permanent site content nor exploits a vulnerability.
23) BFI — Systemic Financial Risk (Admin/Analyst)

Choose BFI Systemic Risk in the left menu. BFI (Bold Financial Intelligence) is a separate page that monitors systemic risk from fund outflows and exchange-rate moves; only admin and analyst roles can open it.|The summary at the top shows the data store, loaded datasets, evidence-chain status and model count. All models are still UNCALIBRATED; results are not investment advice.|SCENARIO runs a contagion/clearing scenario from a reference date and price shocks; it needs loaded fund holdings and prices and warns when data is missing.|DATA uploads TEFAS, BIST, free-float and holdings files; TCMB EVDS exchange rates and other sources are fetched by the server automatically. Signed results from a local node are listed here too. The admin can delete the database here (a confirmation word is required).|SYSTEMIC shows the models, needs, assumptions and limits of the system-level engines and runs a sample Digital Twin.|REPORTS: Open current report, Download PDF, Download Word and Share export it; Archive report stores it. Reports are also archived automatically when the level changes and once a day; past reports open with Open / PDF / Word. Delete (admin only) hides a report from the list; because the record store does not allow rewriting, it is not removed from the database.|Reports are produced in Turkish, English, German, French and Arabic using your interface language; Arabic is laid out right-to-left.|Levels: NORMAL, WATCH and ALARM. ALARM means a large share of funds is showing unusual outflows at the same time, or the exchange rate shocked; a one-week alarm is not a conclusive result.|If automatic sync is enabled on the server, an e-mail (with the report attached) is sent when the level changes.|ADVANCED (JSON) runs the engines directly with a raw request.
voiceClarifyCategory: Which category would you like to analyze: defense, energy, attack, economy, social, advisory, health, multi-domain, BDDK, BTK, or cyber?
voiceAnalysisCreatedNeedTopic: {{category}} analysis created. Please specify the analysis topic.
voiceClarifyAmbiguous: I did not fully understand that command, could you repeat it?
voiceInvalidCommand: I can't safely run that command, please rephrase it.
voiceConfirmLogout: Are you sure you want to log out? Say "yes" to confirm.
errPushUnsupported: This browser does not support push notifications
errPushNotConfigured: Push notifications are not configured on the server
errPushPermissionDenied: Notification permission is blocked — enable it in your browser settings
cyberAnalysisNotConfigured: BCI integration is not yet configured. An administrator must set BCI_BASE_URL / BCI_GATEWAY_SECRET.
cyberScanDeleteConfirm: Delete the scan for {{target}} from all history views? This cannot be undone.
cyberProofDeleteConfirm: Delete Controlled Proof {{proofId}} from all history views? This cannot be undone.
cyberReportDeleteConfirm: Delete the {{type}} report from all history views? This cannot be undone.
cyberScanScopeNote: A scan only starts if the target is covered by an APPROVED authorized scope for the requested class.
cyberNoAssetAnalyses: No reportable analysis was found for this asset.
cyberQuantumIntro: BCI's value is not "using quantum computers" — it is unifying discovery, risk, and remediation decisions in one platform. Quantum compute is one optional backend, used only where a real, measured benefit exists; every org defaults to classical, and nothing below is styled as more certain than what was actually measured.
cyberCryptoScopeNote: TLS/SSH discovery only runs against a target covered by an APPROVED authorized scope — the same authorization bar as starting a scan.
cyberJwtPlaceholder: eyJhbGciOi... (JWT header only is decoded, never verified)
cyberScanWatching: Watching this scan — Findings will open automatically when it completes.
idleLogoutWarningBody: You'll be logged out in {{seconds}}s due to inactivity, to protect your session if you've stepped away.
cyberConfirmArchiveBody: Archive this asset? It will be hidden from the active inventory, but every past scan, finding, and identifier stays fully intact -- you can restore it anytime.
cyberConfirmRestoreBody: Restore this asset to the active inventory?
cyberNoTargetYet: No target registered -- edit is not enough, this asset predates target tracking
cyberScanNoCoverageDetail: No engine actually ran for this target/class combination -- this is not a clean result, it means nothing was analyzed.
cyberSystemDegraded: {{count}} analysis engine(s) unavailable -- some analysis capacity is reduced.
cyberWizDuplicateTarget: This target already exists in the BCI inventory.
cyberWizNoManualOverride: BCI selects engines automatically based on the chosen scan class -- per-engine manual override is not currently supported by the backend.
cyberWizNoExecutableEngine: No executable analysis engine was found for this target and analysis profile.
cyberWizQuantumExplainer: Quantum is not a vulnerability scanner and does not run as part of this scan. It only applies later, as a separate Remediation Optimizer over existing findings across the organization -- shown here is real provider health only.
cyberWizPolicyNotRequired: Not required — runs locally, no external egress
cyberWizNotApplicable: Not applicable — no open findings to optimize
cyberWizEngineRequired: Select at least one engine to continue
cyberEnginesGuideNote: Reference panel — the full engine catalog and its live health, not a scan setup screen. To pick engines for an actual scan, use New Analysis.
cyberQuantumGuideNote: Reference panel — provider health and org policy, not a per-scan selection screen. To pick a compute method for an actual scan, use New Analysis.
cyberWizClassAutoSuggested: BCI switched to {{class}} -- this target has no real engine coverage at a lower class.
cyberControlledProofEvidenceSeparation: Finding Evidence records scanner observations. Controlled Proof of Impact is a separate deterministic validation result.
cyberControlledProofReasonWorkerQueueFai: The Controlled Proof worker job could not be queued.
cyberControlledProofReasonWorkerFailed: The Controlled Proof worker job could not complete.
cyberControlledProofReasonWorkerTimedOut: The Controlled Proof worker job timed out.
cyberControlledProofReasonEdgeDeployment: Public response-body transformation requires an edge code deployment; no safe deployment-free adapter exists.
cyberControlledProofReasonRulesEngineNoB: The provider rules engine cannot safely transform the public HTML response body.
cyberControlledProofReasonSiteDeployment: Displaying the marker requires a site deployment or application code change, which Controlled Proof does not perform.
cyberControlledProofReasonNoSafeSelfExpi: An origin configuration change cannot guarantee absolute self-expiry without a persistent change or preinstalled mechanism.
cyberControlledProofReasonPreinstalledTr: A preinstalled response transformation mechanism is required; none is assumed by Controlled Proof.
cyberControlledProofReasonPersistentCmsC: The available CMS path changes persistent content and is therefore ineligible for Controlled Proof.
cyberControlledProofReasonUnknownInfrast: No verified management path is available for this unknown or custom infrastructure.
cyberControlledProofRejectNotContentImpa: This observation does not contain a verified signal that can affect delivered web content.
cyberControlledProofRejectNoValidator: A content-impact signal exists, but no supported non-destructive response validator can verify it.
cyberControlledProofRejectExactMarker: The bounded marker request completed, but the exact marker was not observed in a supported response.
cyberControlledProofRejectValidatorFaile: The safe validator could not complete; no impact was inferred from the failed execution.
cyberControlledProofRejectUnknown: The candidate did not meet the deterministic Controlled Proof eligibility rules.
cyberControlledProofReasonImpactNotVerif: Security impact was not verified, so public demonstration is not applicable.
cyberControlledProofReasonAdapterMismatc: A configured adapter does not match the detected delivery infrastructure.
cyberControlledProofReasonNoConfiguredAd: No configured public-visibility adapter matches the detected provider.
cyberControlledProofReasonProviderNotCon: The public-visibility provider is not configured for this target.
cyberControlledProofReasonProviderUnavai: The selected public-visibility provider is unavailable.
The provider was unavailable while the public marker was expiring.
cyberControlledProofReasonRouteConflict: A conflicting public route prevents safe marker activation.
cyberControlledProofReasonMarkerNotObser: Independent requests did not observe the exact public marker.
cyberControlledProofReasonExactMarkerNot: The exact validation marker was not observed in the supported response.
cyberControlledProofReasonTransportUnava: The Controlled Proof HTTP transport is unavailable.
cyberControlledProofReasonDeterministicI: The deterministic validator did not verify a security impact path.
cyberControlledProofReasonInvalidTarget: Enter a valid public HTTP or HTTPS target URL.
